title: Deboli to King Stanisław August, St Petersburg, 12 Sep 1786 (AGAD Zbiór Popielów 2, scan 146): first page in table 3865 read in part with our key K3 (partial; partial reading explained)

documents.shelfmark: AGAD Warsaw, Zbiór Popielów (zesp. 12), sygn. 2, scan 146 right
documents.route: Antoni Augustyn Deboli, Polish envoy in St Petersburg -> King Stanisław August

plaintext.source: AGAD AKP 1/11/0/-/269 ('Deboli' 1786-87), scans 253 right - 254: the cabinet's clear of the despatch, opened only after the decoding with the frozen key was hashed; used for the measurement and the restorations, not published here.

transcription.notes: Transcribed once on the scan after the protocol was hashed and before the clear was opened; a fair copy, no corrections; one mark under 1411 not noted; catchword and pencil margin numbers excluded.

system.summary: Table 3865: one-part code of 1-4 digit groups for letters, syllables, endings, words and names; openers 3865 and 9, nulls (7, 12 ...); suffixed variants (a, b, x, z) with their own values; alphabet without j, v, y. No key of the time found.
system.notes: Used by Deboli in 1786-87 beside the older code ZbPop 444 (targets/deboli1787) and tables 9933 and 12282; in 1786 pieces opening '9933' are often 3865 after a heading of 30-55 groups.

prior_solution.where: The cabinet's clear texts of 1786-87 are in AGAD AKP 1/11/0/-/269 (scans 253-254 for this despatch). Unprinted: the IH PAN edition of Deboli's correspondence stops at 1782. No key of 3865 in this repository or elsewhere; catalogue 415 open, no target for it on origin/main (GitHub API, 10 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout obtained the scans and set the rules (each round pre-registered and hashed, thresholds fixed in advance, one measurement per round, held-out ciphers hashed before their clears were opened, strict re-reading rule of 10 Nov 2026). AI agents transcribed, learnt the key, measured, read and summarised. No human palaeographer checked the transcription or the reading.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: ZbPop 2 and 3 sorted by system; table 3865 identified; learning pieces transcribed and paired with their clears in AKP 269.
Key learnt by script on the pairs (K1, K2, K3); held-out rounds R1 0.591, R2 0.598 (against 0.60), R3 0.519 (a corrected draft enciphered in its first state): failed.
R4: key K3 unchanged, one measurement on the held-out fair copy Z2-146: 0.645 of the words of the clear, best of 200 shuffled keys 0.020 (margin 0.625); partial (validated needs 0.85).
Strict re-reading group by group against the clear: 163 certain, 33 probable, 17 restored, 6 unresolved of 219 groups (89.5% without the restored).

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Key K3 learnt on pairs of cipher despatches and the cabinet's clears of the time (AKP 269); one held-out measurement on this page, partial by our protocol. The content is the cabinet's clear (existing); the system, the key table and the checked reading are the contribution.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): 0.645 of words vs at most 0.020 for 200 shuffled keys (margin 0.625), under the 0.85 set in advance: partial. Earlier rounds 0.591, 0.598 and 0.519 failed; on clean copies K3 levels off at 0.63-0.65 (truncated values).

outcome.fraction_read_source: reading/z2_146.md, counted by group: 163 certain + 33 probable = 196 of 219 groups; 17 restored from the clear and 6 unresolved not counted.

texts.label: Deboli, 12 Sep 1786, first page (scan 146 right)
texts.summary: Deboli has handed Vice-Chancellor Ostermann his written observations on Prince Czartoryski's memorandum and sends them to the King, with a passage added for Ambassador Stackelberg, whose agreement is the condition for success in St Petersburg; Sedler presented the memorandum only on the Sunday.

reading_review.note: Re-read group by group as French sentences on 10 Nov 2026 against the clear of the time (AKP 269 scans 253-254), strict rule: certain = K3 value equals the clear letter by letter, sense-only readings probable; 163 certain, 33 probable, 17 restored, 6 unresolved of 219 groups (89.5%); read in part; key K3 partial (0.645 vs 0.020).

outcome.notes: Partial reading explained. Content existing (the cabinet's clear in AKP 269); no images (AGAD: private research only); the clear of the time is not reproduced, only the reading made with the key.
